title: How the radio and his brother brought him saxophone pupils
summary: Most of Waters's pupils came through his brother's bands and the radio broadcasts, including Harry Carney, who left the New England Conservatory to study with him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And he was, what was [ ], and they all beginners. You know, amateurs.
So your brother helped get you students, the radio helped get you students, and that's how you became -

75 per cent of these, at least 75 per cent of the pupils, at least 60 per cent of the pupils I got through my brothers. And the rest, 40 and, in the radio (PS joins in on 'in the radio'), listening to -
And Carney was one of your pupils.
How did he find you, through the radio or through your brother?
No, from the radio. Carney was going to the New England Conservatory. He left the New England Conservatory to come to me.
Were you at the New England Conservatory, or you left, too?
No, not at that point. I -
I stayed about 2 or 3 years at the Conservatory, I took lessons from a graduate of the Conservatory that lived right 'cross the street from me.
You were in Boston for several years after you left the Conservatory then.
